chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa ibn Ubayd, from Yunus, from Abdillah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

"For every person you include in your dependents, whether free or slave, you must pay the Fitrah (Zakat al-Fitr) on their behalf." He said, "Giving the Fitrah before the prayer is superior, and after the prayer it is considered charity."

key_terms.الْفِطْرَة: Zakat al-Fitr, the obligatory alms-giving at the end of Ramadan
key_terms.حُرّ: Free person (as opposed to a slave)
key_terms.عِيَال: Dependents or family members under one's care

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on paying Zakat al-Fitr for dependents and the difference between paying before and after the Eid prayer?
ai.summary: In the *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Shaykh al-Tusi records this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) to clarify the scope of Zakat al-Fitr, extending the obligation to all dependents regardless of their freedom status. The hadith establishes a critical jurisprudential distinction: payment before the Eid prayer fulfills the specific religious duty (Fard), whereas payment after the prayer is valid but reclassified as general voluntary charity (Sadaqah), emphasizing the importance of timely fulfillment in Shia fiqh.
